newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH GROUP THREATENS TO TARGET OLYMPIC ATHLETES.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH GROUP THREATENS TO TARGET OLYMPIC ATHLETES.

text.p: An anonymous group threatened on Monday to target athletes and the public if the Swedish capital city is awarded the 2004 Olympic Games.

The group, whose existence was immediately challenged by police, said in a letter received by the Swedish news agency TT that it was responsible for eight recent fires at sports venues and a bomb explosion last week at Stockholm's Olympic stadium.
The group, calling itself "We Who Built Sweden", said it represented the country's poor and oppressed.

"Eight fires and one explosion have been our warning. We have sought to avoid harm to people. We will continue until the IOC (International Olympic Committee) makes its decision. From then on, human lives will be at stake," the letter said.

"It is us who are burning and blowing up sports facilities. The Swedish people are on their knees -- hospital beds in corridors, slashed dole benefits, reduced pensions and a school where the roof collapses and no one did anything about it.

"We Who Built Sweden have to go cap in hand. At the same time, the elected representatives are content with arranging an Olympic Games which can cost enormous sums. They are putting our security at risk with their Games.

"If Sweden gets the Olympics, everyone who has been involved in the bid process will be our targets. This will include sports people and the public. We have large amounts of explosives, grenade launchers, automatic weapons as well as ammunition.
"We have sufficient to carry out our aims. Do not doubt our decisiveness."
Police discounted the letter, which was signed by the same group that threatened to disrupt Christmas shopping in Swedish cities last year by planting bombs.
Two minor explosive devices were discovered in the western city of Gothenburg, but threats to kill hundreds of people during a Christmas shopping weekend proved to be a hoax.
"I doubt that the letter has been written by the people responsible for the recent attacks," said Stockholm police spokesman Claes Cassel.
"The contents of the letter indicate that it has in fact been written by someone else, but it is difficult to say anything before detectives have been able to analyse it."
Stockholm is competing against Athens, Buenos Aires, Cape Town and Rome for the right to stage the 2004 Games. A decision will be made on September 5.
